title: Cut company tax for small and medium firms, paired with a cash-flow tax
action: Cut the company tax rate to 20 per cent for companies with revenue under $1 billion (28 per cent above), funded in part by a 5 per cent net cash-flow tax on all companies, which lets investment be deducted immediately.
why: Company tax falls on the normal return to investment, so it discourages firms from investing in equipment and new ideas. A lower rate plus a cash-flow tax moves the tax towards above-normal profits and away from investment, and a single threshold at $1 billion replaces the cliff for small firms at $50 million.

evidence.source: Creating a more dynamic and resilient economy: Inquiry report
evidence.quote: The company income tax rate should be cut to 20% for companies with revenue less than $1 billion and be set at 28% for companies with revenue over $1 billion. The cut to company income tax rates will be funded partly by increased tax receipts due to economic growth and partly by a net cashflow tax of 5% to be applied to all companies.

evidence.source: Creating a more dynamic and resilient economy: Inquiry report
evidence.quote: The corporate tax system should better support business dynamism by moving towards a system that promotes investment by reducing the tax on normal returns.

evidence.source: Australia's Future Tax System: Report to the Treasurer, Part One (Henry review)
evidence.quote: The company income tax rate should be reduced to 25 per cent over the short to medium term with the timing subject to economic and fiscal circumstances.

precedents.what: Has taxed companies on a cash-flow basis since 2000, a model later adopted by Latvia, Poland and Georgia (as reported by the Productivity Commission).

tradeoffs: The Productivity Commission designed the package to be revenue-neutral over time, but a net cash-flow tax is new to Australia and would be complex to introduce; the Commission offers simpler options if it is judged too complex.
